analyst_view.overall: Ferencvaros are 3rd with four wins from four in Europe, including 2-0 at AC Milan, and want a top-eight finish; Celje are 25th with 4 points but have won five in a row in all competitions. Ferencvaros lost 3-1 at home to Gyor on Saturday and are without Bamidele Yusuf (banned) and Bence Otvos, both counted (about -17% on their goals for Yusuf); RTV Slovenija adds that backup striker Franko Kovacevic is injured and probably out, which the numbers don't list but matters little with Joseph and Zachariassen expected to start. Celje lose Pijus Sirvys (broken toe) but otherwise report no injury problems, with Seslar, Kvesic and Verbic in form. Celje coach Zoran Zeljkovic says his side's strength is technique rather than physique, so a footballing game is expected in cold Budapest. Italian referee Simone Sozza (about 4.1 cards a game) is already counted, and nothing new is big enough to move the numbers. This evening's check (UEFA, Sporza, foot-africa) adds no new absences: Ferencvaros have won all four European games (11 scored, 3 conceded) and Zachariassen (11 goals) and Celje's Seslar (11 goals) lead the scoring.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals and already take a big slice off Ferencvaros for Yusuf's ban, with Joseph and Zachariassen (11 goals, 9 assists) leading the attack. Kovacevic's injury only thins the bench and Celje, on five straight wins, have scored just 5 in four European games, so I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, already a little higher because Celje have conceded 43 corners in their last six. Ferencvaros should have more of the ball at home, as the 5.4 to 3.9 split shows, while Celje want to pass through rather than go long, so nothing new points either way and I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already trimmed for both sides' calm recent card counts and set by referee Simone Sozza's average record (4.1 a game in 52 games). Both coaches expect a footballing game rather than a physical one, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.3 shots, with Celje's quieter recent shooting (49 in six) already taking 11% off their side. Ferencvaros are close to full strength apart from Yusuf and Otvos (counted) and a backup striker, and Celje miss only Sirvys, so I stay at 25.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, already raised for Ferencvaros's sharp recent finishing (31 on target in six). Joseph, back late from international duty, is still expected to lead the line and Celje's forwards have scored little, so I stay at 9.6.
